links.outcome: Change in documentation and management of psychiatric symptoms after AI scribe deployment
links.effect: Psychiatric intervention (referral, new diagnosis, or antidepressant) less likely in AI-scribed vs contemporaneous unscribed visits (aOR 0.83; 95% CI 0.72-0.95); not different for human scribes (aOR 0.97).
links.quote: In a multiple logistic regression model, likelihood of a psychiatric intervention (referral, new diagnosis, or antidepressant prescription) was significantly lower among AI-scribed visits compared with contemporaneous unscribed visits (adjusted odds ratio, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.72-0.95), but not for human-scribed visits compared with contemporaneous unscribed visits (adjusted odds ratio, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.85-1.11).

links.outcome: Documentation of neuropsychiatric symptoms (RDoC) in AI-scribed vs other notes
links.effect: Estimated RDoC symptom levels in all 6 domains significantly greater in AI-scribed notes compared with other groups.
links.quote: Estimated levels of RDoC symptoms in all 6 domains were significantly greater in the AI-scribed notes compared with other groups.

screen.reason: Evaluates the downstream clinical practice and documentation impacts of real-world deployment of an AI ambient scribe in primary care compared to human/no scribes, but does not test a specific organizational safeguard or deployment practice.
